subject: Stakeholder checkpoints & pilot scope — inference reliability POC
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Jones <emily.jones@nimbustx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Oct 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Stakeholder checkpoints & pilot scope — inference reliability POC

Hi Emily — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Key pain points we heard
- Burst latency spikes at token lengths >1k causing timeouts for live agents
- Token cost unpredictability across peaks — budgeting issues for production
- Model quality drift on edge cases (medical nomenclature) that affects triage accuracy

Goals for the pilot (4 weeks)
- Reduce p95 latency for 1–2k token requests to <150ms on your critical route
- Demonstrate predictable token cost with batching/cache profiles (target: <= $150 per 1M tokens for inference)
- Establish a prompt/eval suite to measure quality regression vs. baseline (target: >= 92% pass on critical prompt set)

Proposed POC scope
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated pool (reserved GPU capacity) in us-west-2
- Workload: 3 production routes (agent assist, triage summarization, and batch-embedding) using a representative subset of your traffic
- Deliverables: latency/cost dashboard, prompt-eval report, runbook with rollback policy

Owners & immediate asks
- Nimbus: Emily (Product) — provide sample traffic slices and security contact for the questionnaire
- Redwood: Rishi (AE) — commercial coordination; Monica (Solutions Eng) — technical kickoff & runbook; Ben (CS) — success criteria & handoff
- Access: Please share an S3 path or transfer method for 200–500 example requests (anonymized). See attached "shared-data-list.csv" for the preferred schema.

Attachments & links
- mutual-action-plan.xlsx (proposed timeline + milestone owners)
- shared-data-list.csv (sample schema + anonymization checklist)
- Collaboration doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-example

Proposed next steps
1) Emily: confirm security contact and agree to data transfer method by Wed 10/03
2) Both teams: calendar 30–45 minute kickoff (suggest Thu 10/04 10:00 PT)
3) Redwood: share pilot runbook draft within 24 hours of kickoff

If that aligns, I’ll lock the kickoff time and send a calendar invite with an agenda. Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — I’ve put together the IAM & egress checklist and a short runbook stub. Highlights below; full checklist attached as access-checklist.md.

Quick highlights (from access-checklist.md)
- IAM: create a pilot role (redwood-pilot-infer-role) with s3:GetObject limited to the provided bucket first, then narrow to prefixes after validation
- Network: allow outbound HTTPS egress to s3.amazonaws.com and the Redwood control-plane IP ranges (see runbook) for initial provisioning; recommend VPC peering for sustained traffic
- Secrets: provide a temporary transfer token; we recommend rotating the token after ingestion and rotating again post-POC

Runbook steps we’ll cover at kickoff
1) Validate sample traffic (Sanity check on 200–500 anonymized requests)
2) Deploy model variant + batching profile to Redwood Dedicated pool
3) Run synthetic load to confirm p95 latency targets
4) Execute prompt-eval harness and capture baseline metrics

I attached access-checklist.md and updated mutual-action-plan.xlsx with the task owners and dates. I’m good for Thu 10/04 10:00 PT for the kickoff.

—Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
